note_on_method: Each venue page rests on the City of Long Beach's pickleball page, which gives the park one line with an address, a count and the word dedicated or dual-striped, plus the park's own directory page, where one exists, for the acreage, the amenity list and the history the City wrote itself. Two venues, Junipero Beach and Bayshore Park, have no park page and rest on the one line alone. The US Census address geocoder and OpenStreetMap supply the county and the postcode. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Eight dedicated pickleball courts in the north of Long Beach. The City's line pairs DeForest Park, 6255 DeForest Ave., with "8 dedicated courts". That is the largest dedicated set in the city, and dedicated means pickleball courts rather than a tennis court wearing a second set of lines.

The park's own page is titled DeForest Park and Wetlands and lists "Pickleball Courts" among its amenities, alongside a basketball court, a community centre, futsal courts, a playground, a softball field, a sand volleyball court and restrooms. The site is 49.6 acres in all, of which the City owns 15. The remaining 34.91 acres is the DeForest Nature Trail, restored as freshwater wetlands and reopened on 30 June 2018.
slots.getting_there:
6255 DeForest Ave, Long Beach, CA 90805, Los Angeles County. The address comes from the City's pickleball page; the park's own page prints no street address. The US Census address geocoder matched it at house-number level as "6255 DE FOREST AVE" in the incorporated place Long Beach city.

The City publishes nothing about parking. Restrooms are in the amenity list, and the City's history counts two.
slots.what_to_expect:
Eight dedicated courts is a rotation rather than a queue, and with no tennis lines to argue over, a court here is a pickleball court whenever you arrive. The City's rule for its park courts applies: "NO reservations at this time", first come, first served.

Hours are the clearest in the city: "Park Hours: Dawn to Dusk". That is also the limit. The City's history lights the four tennis courts and says nothing about lighting the pickleball courts, so pickleball lighting is recorded as unknown and daylight is the plan.

No price is stated and no surface, and the City never calls these courts indoor or outdoor. Nothing is published about when they are busy.

faqs.a: Eight, in the City's words "8 dedicated courts", the largest dedicated set in Long Beach and pickleball courts in their own right rather than lines on a tennis court.
"Park Hours: Dawn to Dusk" on the park's own page. DeForest is the one Long Beach park whose page states hours for the park rather than for a community-centre programme.
Not stated. The City's park courts are first come, first served, which is a play format, and no price is published either way.

slots.description:
Four dedicated pickleball courts on the west side of Long Beach, stated with a phone number: the City's line gives 1545 W. 31st St., "4 dedicated pickleball courts" and "Call 562.570.1675."

The park's own page lists "Pickleball Courts" in an amenity list that runs to baseball fields, a basketball court, a community centre, a gym, picnic areas, a playground, a swimming pool, a softball field, tennis courts, volleyball and restrooms. The City calls it "One of the more intensively active recreational parks in the City". The land was bought from the Moulton Estate in February 1925, the pool was added in 1961 and the gymnasium in 1980.

The US Census address geocoder matched "1545 W 31ST ST" at house-number level in the incorporated place Long Beach city.

The City publishes nothing about parking. Restrooms are in the amenity list.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four dedicated courts, enough for two games at once, and because they are dedicated a court here is a pickleball court whenever you arrive. First come, first served under the City's rule, "NO reservations at this time".

The hours printed on the park page are not court hours. They are programme hours for the community centre, ending "Saturday & Sunday: Closed", and these pages do not attach them to the courts, which the City does not schedule.

Lighting is not stated for the pickleball courts. The history lights one baseball field and the overlay soccer field, and none of that names pickleball, so the courts' lighting is recorded as unknown. No price, no surface, and no indoor or outdoor word.

faqs.a: Four, in the City's words "4 dedicated pickleball courts", which makes them pickleball courts in their own right rather than lines on tennis.
Not stated for the courts. The hours on the park page are community-centre programme hours, ending with "Saturday & Sunday: Closed", and they are not carried across to the courts.

faqs.q: Is there a number to call?
faqs.a: Yes. The City's line ends "Call 562.570.1675.", the one park line on its pickleball page that gives a phone number.

slots.description:
Twelve pickleball courts in central Long Beach, and the twelve is the City's own arithmetic. Its line calls Veterans Park, 101 E. 28th St., a "Hybrid location: 8 pickleball courts on 1 tennis court and 4 dedicated pickleball courts." Eight are lines on a single tennis court; four are pickleball courts in their own right. That makes Veterans the largest published venue in Long Beach by count, and the one with the most ambiguity built into its number.

The park's own page does not mention pickleball at all. Its amenity list carries basketball courts, a baseball field, a community centre, picnic areas, a playground, a soccer field, "Tennis Court", a volleyball/soccer court and restrooms. The City's history records a 14.3-acre site "between 28th and Spring Streets", named Veterans Memorial Park on 19 August 1952 and completed in April 1958.
slots.getting_there:
101 E 28th St, Long Beach, CA 90806, Los Angeles County. The address is from the City's pickleball page; the park page prints none, though its history places the park between 28th and Spring Streets. The US Census address geocoder matched "101 E 28TH ST" at house-number level in the incorporated place Long Beach city.

The City publishes nothing about parking. Restrooms are in the amenity list, and the history mentions a freestanding restroom. The hours printed on the page do not say what they govern, and these pages do not attach them to the courts.
slots.what_to_expect:
Twelve courts on paper and something between four and twelve in practice. The four dedicated courts are pickleball courts whenever you arrive. The other eight are "8 pickleball courts on 1 tennis court", and the City's rule for shared courts governs them: first come, first served, "and court signage regarding shared use must be observed". If a tennis game is on that court, the eight are not available, and the City publishes no schedule saying when that will be.

The City lights the softball, baseball and soccer fields in its history and says nothing about lighting the tennis court or the pickleball courts, so lighting is recorded as unknown and daylight is the plan. No price is stated, no surface, no court hours, and no indoor or outdoor word.

faqs.a: Twelve, the City's own sum: "8 pickleball courts on 1 tennis court and 4 dedicated pickleball courts." Four are dedicated; eight are lines on one tennis court.
The City's word for a park with both kinds of court. Here it means four dedicated pickleball courts and one tennis court striped for eight more, shared under court signage.
Not stated. First come, first served is a play format, not a price, and the City publishes no fee either way for its park courts.

slots.description:
Two dedicated pickleball courts on East Ocean Boulevard, in the City's one sentence about them: 2100 E. Ocean Blvd., "2 dedicated pickleball courts on repurposed half basketball court."

That line is the whole of the City's record. There is no Junipero Beach page in the City's park directory, so there is no acreage, no amenity list and no history to draw on, and this page does not borrow any from elsewhere. What the line does give is unusual: a count, an address, the word dedicated, and the ground's previous life. A repurposed half basketball court is the nearest thing to a surface history the City writes for any Long Beach venue.
slots.getting_there:

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms here, because it publishes nothing about the venue beyond the one line. Those gaps are recorded as gaps rather than filled from a map.
slots.what_to_expect:
Two courts, dedicated, first come, first served. The City's rule applies as everywhere in its parks, "NO reservations at this time", and with both courts dedicated there is no tennis or basketball to share them with, whatever the ground used to be.

With two courts there is no rotation to join. One match at a time on each, and if both are taken you wait. It is a place for a game you bring with you.

What the City does not say is almost everything else. No hours, no lighting either way, no price, and no surface beyond "repurposed half basketball court", which describes the history of the slab rather than what it is coated with now.

faqs.a: Two, in the City's words "2 dedicated pickleball courts on repurposed half basketball court". Two courts is a game, not a rotation.
Not stated. Junipero Beach has no page in the City's park directory, and the pickleball page's line gives a count and an address only.
Not stated. The City's park courts are first come, first served, which is a play format, and no price is published either way.

slots.description:
Three pickleball courts on a shared sports court in the western section of El Dorado Regional Park. The City's line gives 2800 N. Studebaker Rd. and "3 pickleball courts on a shared sports court."

The park is 272.5 acres, "Area I of El Dorado Regional Park", and the City describes it as "a spacious community center, night-lighted basketball and multi-use courts, softball and soccer fields, skate park, four group picnic sites available for reservation, a disc golf course, a tennis center, playground equipment and a duck pond". The amenity list carries "Multi-use Courts" and "Tennis Court" but no pickleball line; the three courts appear only on the pickleball page.

The tennis centre in that description is the El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center, at the same address, with eight courts of its own and a separate page here.
slots.getting_there:
2800 N Studebaker Rd, Long Beach, CA 90815, Los Angeles County. The City's pickleball page writes "2800 N. Studebaker Rd."; the park page's address block writes "2800 Studebaker Road". The US Census address geocoder matched "2800 N STUDEBAKER RD" at house-number level in the incorporated place Long Beach city.

The same address is published for the El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center, and the two are different venues. The City publishes nothing about parking at either. Restrooms are in the park's amenity list, and the page gives a phone number, (562) 570-3225.
slots.what_to_expect:
Three courts on a shared sports court, first come, first served, with the City's rider that "court signage regarding shared use must be observed". Three is an odd number for pickleball: one game and a court spare, or a small group rotating. Because the court is shared, what it is set up for when you arrive is not something the City schedules.

Lighting is the interesting gap. The City says the park has "night-lighted basketball and multi-use courts", but whether the shared sports court the pickleball sits on is one of them is not something it says, so lighting is recorded as unknown. The hours on the page are the community centre's and are not attached to the courts here.

No price is stated, no surface, and no indoor or outdoor word.

faqs.a: Three, in the City's words "3 pickleball courts on a shared sports court". The park page itself lists multi-use courts and no pickleball line.

faqs.q: Is this the same as the El Dorado tennis centre?
faqs.a: No. Same address, two venues. These are three park courts under the first-come rule; the El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center has eight lit courts, a price and its own hours.
Not stated. First come, first served is the City's play format for its park courts, and no price is published either way.

slots.description:
Three pickleball courts on East Ocean Boulevard. The City's line gives "5415 E. Ocean" and "1 dedicated court, 2 dual-striped". Three is the City's own arithmetic. One court is pickleball and nothing else; two are pickleball lines painted over another sport's, and shared.

That line is the whole City record. There is no Bayshore Park page in the City's park directory, so there is no acreage, no amenity list and no history here, and this page does not import any.

What the line does settle is the kind of court. Bayshore has the same shape as the City's two hybrid parks, Veterans and Marina Vista, in miniature: one court you can count on, two you share. The City does not say what the other sport on the dual-striped pair is, so this page does not either.

Ocean" with no street type, and the US Census address geocoder matched "5415 E OCEAN BLVD" at house-number level in the incorporated place Long Beach city. The Boulevard is the resolver's; the number and the direction are the City's.

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms here, because it publishes no page for the park.
slots.what_to_expect:
One court that is always pickleball and two that may not be. The dedicated court is yours when you get there. The two dual-striped courts are shared with whatever else is painted on them, under the City's rule that "court signage regarding shared use must be observed", and the City does not say what the other sport is or when it has priority.

So Bayshore is one game guaranteed and a second or third if the striped courts are clear. There is no rotation to join at three courts.

No hours are stated, no lighting either way, no price, no surface and no indoor or outdoor word. Every one of those is a gap in a record that is one line long.

faqs.a: Three, the City's own sum of "1 dedicated court, 2 dual-striped". One is pickleball only; two are shared with another sport's lines.

faqs.q: Why does the address read differently from the City's?
faqs.a: The City writes "5415 E. Ocean" with no street type. The Census address file resolves it as E Ocean Blvd, and that is what is published, with the City's number and direction.
Not stated. The City's park courts are first come, first served, which is a play format, and no price is published either way.

slots.description:
Eight pickleball courts, four dedicated and four dual-striped, in an 18.2-acre park in the south-east of the city. The City calls it a "Hybrid location: 4 dedicated pickleball courts and 4 dual-striped courts for either tennis or pickleball." Eight is the sum of the City's own two figures.

The park's own page says "True to Marina Vista's name, the park overlooks the water and provides a scenic atmosphere", and lists two soccer fields, tennis courts and a softball diamond. Its amenity list has no pickleball line; the courts appear only on the pickleball page. Park development began in 1982, and the tennis court "was completed" in 1998. The park hosts Municipal Band concerts.
slots.getting_there:
5355 Eliot St, Long Beach, CA 90814, Los Angeles County. The City's pickleball page locates the park by cross streets only, "Colorado St. & Santiago"; the park's own page gives "5355 Eliot St.", and that is the address published. OpenStreetMap matched it at house-number level in Long Beach, while the US Census geocoder answered "5355 E ELIOT ST", adding a compass direction the City does not write.

The City publishes nothing about parking. The amenity list has no restroom line, but the history records that "The freestanding restroom building was added in 1992".
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts you can count on and four you share. The dedicated four are pickleball courts whenever you arrive. The dual-striped four are "for either tennis or pickleball", and under the City's rule, first come, first served with "court signage regarding shared use must be observed", a tennis player who arrived first has the court.

So Marina Vista is two games guaranteed and a rotation of eight if the tennis side is quiet, and the City does not say when that is.

No hours are stated for the park or the courts, and the courts cannot be reserved. Lighting is not stated for any court here, so it is recorded as unknown and daylight is the plan. No price, no surface, no indoor or outdoor word.

faqs.a: Eight, the City's own sum: "4 dedicated pickleball courts and 4 dual-striped courts for either tennis or pickleball." Four are pickleball only; four are shared with tennis.
Both are the City's. The pickleball page gives cross streets, "Colorado St. & Santiago"; the park page gives "5355 Eliot St.", and the street address is the one published here.
Not stated. First come, first served is the City's play format for its park courts, and no price is published either way.

slots.description:
Eight lit pickleball courts at the City's tennis centre inside El Dorado Park, stated twice: "El Dorado Tennis Center offers eight shared-use pickleball courts" on the City's pickleball page, and "8 Pickleball Courts, Fully Lighted" in the centre's own amenity list, which also runs to "15 Lighted Courts", ball machines, a pro shop and "NO LIGHT FEES!"

The centre's page names it the El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center and says it "is managed for the City of Long Beach by BTG Tennis & Pickleball". Shared-use means the eight are tennis courts in pickleball configuration during the blocks the centre allots to pickleball, not courts that are pickleball all day.

It is the one Long Beach venue where the City states lighting, the one with a price, and the one with a schedule.
slots.getting_there:
2800 Studebaker Road, Long Beach, CA 90815, Los Angeles County, as the centre's page writes it; the City's pickleball page writes "2800 N. Studebaker Rd." OpenStreetMap matched the address as the centre writes it, while the US Census geocoder answered "2800 N STUDEBAKER RD", adding a direction. It is the same address as El Dorado Park West, whose three courts are a different venue under different rules.

The City publishes nothing about parking. The centre's page lists no restroom, and that is recorded as unknown. The phone number is (562) 425-0553, and the page says "Reservations can be made up to one week in advance."
slots.what_to_expect:
A priced, scheduled, lit game, the one of its kind in Long Beach. The City's rates: "$5 per person for drop-in play (up to three hours), while private pickleball court reservations are $10 per court per hour." Drop-in pickleball, as the page stood when read, ran "Tuesday and Thursday mornings from 8 to 11 am, and Friday evenings from 6 to 9pm", and the City says future offerings "will expand drop-in play on every weekday morning from 8 to 11 am".

The centre is open Monday to Friday 7 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. and weekends 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Its page also prints court fees of $10 and $15 an hour by time of day without naming a sport; the pickleball rates published here come from the City's pickleball page.

The courts are "Fully Lighted" with "NO LIGHT FEES", so the Friday evening block is the after-dark pickleball the City puts in writing. Surface is not stated.

faqs.a: "$5 per person for drop-in play (up to three hours)" and "$10 per court per hour" for a private pickleball reservation, in the City's words. The centre's page says there are no light fees.
Tuesday and Thursday mornings 8 to 11 a.m. and Friday evenings 6 to 9 p.m. when the page was read, with the City saying it will expand to every weekday morning.

faqs.q: Is this the same as El Dorado Park West?
faqs.a: No. Same address, two venues. The park's three courts on a shared sports court are first come, first served; the centre's eight are priced, scheduled and lit.
